mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises the cost of capital and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met over a 10-year out-of-sample period.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when this trigger is active.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes over a 15-year sample.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: No statistically significant negative correlation (p > 0.05) between INDPRO contraction events and subsequent 20-day S&P 500 returns in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a fall in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) below 1.5% over two months signals a restrictive monetary policy coinciding with subdued inflation, which increases discount rates without offsetting cost pressures, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: restrictive monetary policy with low inflation
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in real personal income (PAYEMS) and a decline in the housing starts index (HOUST) by more than 10% over two months signals a shift from housing investment to other consumption, which temporarily boosts non-durable demand but weakens capital-intensive sectors, producing mixed but generally positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises AND HOUST falls > -10% over 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 0.5% month-over-month for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of sustained employment growth.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above 3% combined with a federal funds rate below 1% for three months signals a late-cycle demand expansion with accommodative policy, which elevates equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY > 3% AND FEDFUNDS < 1% for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during triggered late-cycle episodes.
